items.title: Walter "Furry" Lewis Interview, 1968-09-02
items.q: I didn't know anything personal about him. Outside of, we'd get together and have a little ball and get drunk and, know, like that.

ctx.x: I got it on tape and my Californian friend and I listened to this record, just listened to the music and the lyrics sounded so interesting. He was thinking about sitting in a jail or so. And he said they built up a new jail on Tulane and Broad. And we didn't know anything about them. These records were made in Jackson, Mississippi. But Tulane, Broad is just a common name for a spree, but Tulane sounded very much like New Orleans. And we got out the map and found this criminal. Tulane and Broad. Tulane and Broad.…

No, let me see. I don't know what his real name was. That was his nickname. A lot of them guys just knew him about his nickname. You don't know his real name. I don't know what his real name was. But they used to call him Stormy Weather. He used to boogie woogie. He used to love to play the boogie when he'd sing all the little rally blues, you know? Yeah. I don't know too much about him, but outside of, you know, I didn't know anything personal about him. Outside of, we'd get together and have a little ball and…
Do you think he was from New Orleans? Yeah, he was. He was from New Orleans. Maybe, uh, it took, uh, tell me more about him.
